variants.headline: Building project badly behind schedule
variants.sub: Construction of a building project is severely delayed in {colony}.
variants.body:
A building project is badly behind schedule in {colony}. The delay is the established failure against its timetable, not a complete account of why it occurred. Readers considering {target} should distinguish that known position from invented shortages, contractor disputes or financial consequences not supplied in the report.

Workers know that a timetable can be treated as somebody else's promise and somebody else's problem. Labour should resist any account that makes ordinary people invisible in the question of delivery. A serious delay warrants attention without assuming that workers caused it or that speed should override decent conditions.

We fault {target} over the standard of delivery. A schedule is not an ornament to a project, and serious lateness is a proper reason to question the adequacy of the stewardship involved. Ordinary lives should be the measure, not a convenient afterthought.

variants.headline: Construction timetable falls seriously short
variants.sub: A colony building project has fallen badly behind its schedule.
variants.body:
A construction schedule is an expectation about when something will be ready. A building project in the colony is falling badly short of that expectation. In assessing {target}, the question is responsible delivery, without assuming either the cause of the delay or a new date for completion.

Workers know that a timetable can be treated as somebody else's promise and somebody else's problem. Labour should resist any account that makes ordinary people invisible in the question of delivery. A serious delay warrants attention without assuming that workers caused it or that speed should override decent conditions.

variants.headline: A project waits beyond its schedule
variants.sub: A building project in the colony is badly behind schedule.
variants.body:
The colony has a building project severely behind schedule. The gap between planned timing and delivery deserves scrutiny in its own right. For {target}, responsibility should be considered without attaching an unreported overrun, contractual penalty or abandoned purpose to the fact of the project's lateness.

Workers know that a timetable can be treated as somebody else's promise and somebody else's problem. Labour should resist any account that makes ordinary people invisible in the question of delivery. A serious delay warrants attention without assuming that workers caused it or that speed should override decent conditions.
